basis: Seeding-year budget assumes 2.5 tons from two cuts against 4 tons for an established stand
The established-stand budget charges one third of the establishment cost each year, so a stand is kept at least three years after it is seeded
The LSU budget is a 4-year rotation: plant cane and two stubble (ratoon) crops, then fallow; the per-acre cost spreads planting and fallow over the rotation
source: LSU AgCenter 2025 Sugarcane Enterprise Budgets, Table 1A

basis: Plant cane and two stubble (ratoon) crops, then a fallow year before replanting: the 4-year rotation of the LSU budget, whose per-acre cost spreads planting and fallow over the harvested years
source: LSU AgCenter 2025 Sugarcane Enterprise Budgets, Table 1A

basis: At least three years from one sugarbeet crop to the next (beet, two other crops, beet): NDSU advises three years or longer between beet crops for the root pathogens and a three- to four-year rotation for rhizomania; on CSB fields that grew beets in 2025, 6.9 % had grown them one or two years before (CDL, which overstates short returns through misclassification)
source: Ashley, Bergman and Eckhoff 2001 (NDSU Dickinson REC); NDSU Sugarbeet Production Guide A1698-26; Wyoming Extension B1063 (five or more years for soil-borne fungi); USDA NASS CDL 2018-2025 on the CSB field sample

basis: At least three years from one flax crop to the next: NDSU advises flax no more than once in three years in any rotation (Fusarium wilt, pasmo, root rots); on CSB fields that grew flax in 2025, 4.2 % had grown it one or two years before (CDL)
source: NDSU Extension A1038, Flax Production in North Dakota; USDA NASS CDL 2018-2025 on the CSB field sample
